links.targetTitle: All four Risk Curation instances share a single Curator mult

title: The instance tree is network-scoped first, so the same protocol is approved and reviewed separately per chain
content:
After the Ethereum Mainnet venues the tree opens a sibling: "The Base Instances of the Spark Liquidity Layer with `Active` Status are stored herein" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.2), immediately followed by its own Morpho section (.2.1) and the Base - Morpho Blue USDC ERC4626 Vault instance (.2.1.1).

The hierarchy is therefore network → protocol → instance, not protocol → network. Every venue is re-approved, re-parameterised and re-reviewed for each chain it runs on, and there is no shared 'Morpho' object that both chains inherit from.

That is the right decomposition for the actual risks. A protocol deployment on Base has different contracts, different liquidity, different bridge dependencies and different governance latency from its mainnet counterpart, and a limit sized for one says nothing about the other.

The verdicts confirm the independence is real rather than clerical: Base Morpho Blue reads "**`Covered`**" (.2.1.1.1) while all three Ethereum Morpho instances read "**`Pending`**". The same protocol name carries opposite review states on two chains — which is coherent under per-chain assessment, and would look like a contradiction to anyone summarising coverage by protocol. The Base instance also sharpens the field name to `Token Address (ERC4626 Vault)` (.2.1.1.2.2.1), a small sign that the schema is still being refined as the newer subtrees are written.
description: Base opens its own subtree with its own Morpho section, and Base Morpho Blue is marked Covered while the Ethereum Morpho instances are all Pending — one protocol, two independent risk verdicts.
